items.answer: Daiyu sneered, "I knew it. Unless the others have turned them down, I'm not getting anything."

items.text: 賈母道：「讀的是什麼書，不過是認得兩個字，不是睜眼的瞎子罷了！」
items.answer: Grandmother Jia said, "What books? They merely know a few characters, that's all. They're not blind, at least."

errors.evidence: They're not blind, at least.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: Phoenix said, "I've been telling you all day long that you're too soft. Letting the household servants get away with this kind of thing—how could it be tolerated?"

errors.evidence: Phoenix said
errors.why: 鳳姐 is rendered as 'Phoenix' without explanation; the standard rendering is Xifeng (Wang Xifeng), which the reader knows.

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day long
errors.why: 成日家 means 'constantly, day in day out'; 'all day long' reads as one long stretch rather than a habitual complaint, though the meaning is largely kept.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: "Feng Jie said, 'I've been telling you all day long that you're far too soft. Let the household get away with this sort of thing and where will it end?'"

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day long
errors.why: 成日家 means 'constantly/always', not a literal stretch of one day, so this reads as one day's scolding instead of a habitual complaint.

errors.evidence: Feng Jie
errors.why: 鳳姐 is the familiar character Xifeng. Rendering it as 'Feng Jie' keeps the nickname as a form of address, which is acceptable but less consistent for the reader.

errors.evidence: Let the household get away with this sort of thing
errors.why: 家裡人 means household servants, not the household as a whole; here it is left vague.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day long

Wait, I must not use the pinyin "Ping'er" in English prose; the name should be preserved as pinyin, which is allowed for names, but I should avoid stray labels. Here is the clean translation:

Ping'er laughed and said, "'Where it is possible to let people off, one should spare them.' We may as well overlook a few things and let it go."

items.text: 祖師聞言，咄的一聲，跳下高臺，手持戒尺，指定悟空道：「你這猢猻，這般不學，那般不學，卻待怎麼？」

errors.why: 戒尺 is a disciplinary rod or ferule. "Teacher's ruler" is vague and loses the disciplinary sense, though it is not wrong enough to mislead.

items.text: 祖師聞言，咄的一聲，跳下高臺，手持戒尺，指定悟空道：「你這猢猻，這般不學，那般不學，卻待怎麼？」

errors.why: 戒尺 is a disciplinary ruler or rod; "clapper" is an odd, inaccurate term and obscures that it is a rod for punishing.

errors.evidence: gave a sharp "Ha!"
errors.why: 咄 is an angry rebuking exclamation ("Tut!"/"Hmph!"); "Ha!" suggests laughter.

items.text: 這猴王也是他一竅通時百竅通，當時習了口訣，自修自煉，將七十二般變化都學成了。
items.answer: The Monkey King, too, was one of those who, once one orifice opens, have all the rest open as well. He at once learned the secret formula, practiced and refined it on his own, and before long had mastered all seventy-two transformations.

errors.evidence: before long had mastered
errors.why: The source does not say how long mastery took; "before long" adds a time frame, though the sense is close.
